extracted.intended_audience: authors of systematic reviews (Cochrane review authors) and those collecting/extracting data for intervention reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, collecting, extracting, managing, and sharing data for systematic reviews of interventions, including which sources to search, what data items to collect, how to design and pilot data collection forms, and how to handle reliability, discrepancies, and special sources (CSRs, registries, IPD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Studies (not reports) as the unit of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: In a systematic review, studies rather than reports of studies are the principal unit of interest; multiple reports of the same study must be identified and linked so the study (not each report) is counted once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link multiple reports together before or after extraction; do not treat multiple reports as multiple studies. Use trial characteristics (registration numbers, authors, sponsors, setting, intervention details, participant numbers, dates) and, when uncertain, correspond with study authors or sponsors. Secondary reports should not be discarded as they may contain valuable design or conduct information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider strengths and limitations of data sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Review authors should consider which data sources may be available and which may contain the most useful information for the review; these considerations should be described in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A comprehensive search is resource-intensive but necessary. Begin accessing CSRs and contacting investigators early. Describe which sources were prioritized and why in the protocol. Use Table 5.2.a as a framework for weighing strengths/limitations of each source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use journal articles for most data but recognise limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal articles are the source of the majority of data included in systematic reviews, but may be incomplete and may represent only some aspects of a study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multiple articles per study (design, main results, other results). Be alert to selective reporting, missing outcomes (especially harms), and limited method detail; seek supplementary sources where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat conference abstracts with caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference abstracts are commonly available but provide highly variable reliability, accuracy, and level of detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They can help identify unpublished studies but often lack necessary detail for meta-analysis and can risk double-counting if not linked to full reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine errata and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Errata, letters, and retraction statements can provide important information about study weaknesses and potential retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine relevant retraction statements and errata for information. Retrieve errata in database searches and include details in citation data. If a publication is retracted or unreliable, consider exclusion and note the reason in excluded studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search trial registries (e.g., ClinicalTrials.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial registries catalogue trials and are important for identifying trials, comparing planned vs published outcomes, and obtaining efficacy and safety data not elsewhere available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registries can link multiple sources via unique registration numbers but are limited to more recent studies and may be incomplete or inaccurate; they may report only thresholds for harms or not reflect protocol changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clinical study reports (CSRs) when possible
rubrics_metrics.description: CSRs contain comprehensive, unabridged descriptions of clinical trials (protocols, SAPs, appendices) and often include more detail on methods and results than public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSRs can be thousands of pages and are often hard to obtain; request from regulators (e.g., EMA) or repositories. They are particularly valuable for harms and detailed methods, but obtaining and analysing them is time-consuming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use regulatory reviews as supplementary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory reviews (FDA, EMA) summarise CSRs and related documents and often provide reanalyses and useful details about trials submitted for marketing approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory reviews may be limited to initial approvals, not standardised in format, and less available for older or off-label uses. Consider freedom-of-information requests where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek individual participant data (IPD) when advantageous
rubrics_metrics.description: IPD are participant-level datasets obtained from investigators or open repositories and permit flexible reanalysis, standardization, and additional subgroup analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPD require time and expertise to obtain and analyse, may not always add new information beyond aggregate reports or CSRs, and need clear data usage agreements and consideration of ethics and legality.

rubrics_metrics.name: MECIR: Examine errata (C48)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory expectation to examine any relevant retraction statements and errata for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errata may reveal limitations or fatal flaws that could lead to exclusion; ensure errata are retrieved in searches and tied to citation data.

rubrics_metrics.name: MECIR: Collate multiple reports (C42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory expectation to collate multiple reports of the same study so that each study is the unit of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat multiple reports as separate studies. Choose and justify which report to use for results. Use as many trial characteristics as possible to link reports and contact authors if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: MECIR: Obtain unpublished data (C49)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly desirable to seek key unpublished information missing from reports of included studies by contacting study authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact authors to obtain missing details for risk of bias, interventions, outcomes, and results (including subgroup breakdowns). Provide specific requests or short data collection forms to facilitate responses; request IPD explicitly if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and describe what data to collect (data definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are any information about (or derived from) a study, including methods, participants, setting, interventions, outcomes, results, publications, and investigators; the data to be sought should be planned in advance and described in the protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Involve consumers/stakeholders to ensure relevance. Collected data should support tables/figures, risk-of-bias assessments, and syntheses. Familiarise with PRISMA and reporting guidelines to include relevant elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing studies (MECIR C44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory to collect characteristics of included studies in sufficient detail to populate a 'Characteristics of included studies' table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include participants, interventions, comparators, outcomes, and study design. Present basic characteristics for readers and for use in synthesis and applicability assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record data-extraction metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect metadata about data extraction: name(s) of data extractors, date of extraction, and identification features of each report used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording provenance helps transparency and reproducibility; link extracted items clearly to source documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm eligibility and reasons for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the eligibility decision for each study and record reasons for exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep clear records to populate excluded studies sections and to justify inclusion/exclusion decisions in the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect detailed study methods to assess bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect study design features (parallel, factorial, crossover, cluster), number of centres, recruitment methods, enrolment dates, follow-up length, random sequence generation, allocation concealment, masking, confounding controls, and methods to handle missing data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full descriptions are required for risk-of-bias assessments (see related chapters). Collect statistical unit of analysis and statistical methods used for extracted effect estimates, and sources of funding/conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect participants and setting characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect participant eligibility criteria, baseline characteristics (age, sex, comorbidity, socio-economic status), setting (care setting, region), diagnostic criteria, and other characteristics relevant to applicability and effect modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to summarize characteristics for whole study or by intervention group. Collect formats consistently where possible; collect setting and timing information if relevant to applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect detailed intervention descriptions (use TIDieR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect components, delivery routes, doses, timing, frequency, protocols, duration, staff qualifications, co-interventions, definition of control groups, and implementation factors; use TIDieR to structure descriptions to permit replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex or non-pharmacological interventions, collect greater detail (who delivered, format, timing). Summarize interventions in 'Characteristics of included studies' and consider logic models or diagrams for multi-component interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect information on intervention integrity (fidelity/adherence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect data on the degree to which the intervention was implemented as planned (adherence, fidelity), including whether tailoring or modifications occurred and strategies to assess fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on integrity helps distinguish poor intervention design from poor implementation. Whether lack of integrity biases estimates depends on whether interest is in assignment effect or adherence effect; collect process data where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect process evaluation information when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When important, collect whether trials accounted for or measured key process factors and whether trials that addressed integrity showed different effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process evaluations use mixed methods; Chapter 21 guides their inclusion. Process data can identify mechanisms and factors influencing effectiveness and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect outcomes using five elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each outcome, collect five elements: (1) outcome domain/title, (2) measurement tool/instrument (including scale details), (3) specific metric (e.g. post-intervention value or change), (4) method of aggregation (mean/SD, proportions), and (5) timing of measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect outcomes defined in the protocol in detail; a complete list of all outcomes measured can help assess risk of bias due to missing outcome data. Consider special needs for economic and patient-reported outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect adverse effects in appropriate detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect harms data, noting whether harms were collected systematically or non-systematically; capture coding systems used, thresholds, and denominators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically collected harms are handled like efficacy outcomes. Non-systematic collection is prone to selective reporting. Collect coding terminology/version (e.g., MedDRA), case definitions, severity, and denominators where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect results for each group at each time point
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group and outcome/time point, collect numbers randomized and analysed, withdrawals and reasons, summary data (2x2 tables, means/SDs), and between-group effect estimates with precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also collect subgroup-specific data if subgroup analyses are planned. Retain provenance of original reported numbers and any calculated values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect miscellaneous study information
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect authors' key conclusions, references to other studies, correspondence required, and miscellaneous comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items can inform interpretation and decisions about contacting authors for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design data collection forms to support planned outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop data collection forms guided by planned tables and figures, making forms easy to use and to collect sufficient, unambiguous data that faithfully represent the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot forms, provide coding instructions, and involve stakeholders in form design. Retain provenance and a clear distinction between source data and calculated data. Consider software that maintains calculation history rather than hand calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select data collection tools thoughtfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider rationale, feasibility, resource needs, compatibility with planned analyses, and whether to use standardised/shared tools or bespoke forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance ease-of-use with capturing sufficient detail; standardising tools across review teams can streamline production. Consider databases/spreadsheets that permit export for cleaning and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who should extract data and extraction methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether extraction will be done by single extractor, independent double extraction, content experts, or methodologists, and document the approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence suggests single extraction yields more errors than double extraction. Plan how disagreements will be resolved and whether extraction will be done by content experts, methodologists, or both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide training, pilot testing, and coding instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Train extractors, pilot test data collection forms, and provide coding instructions to improve reliability and reduce errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot testing and training should be documented; coding manuals help standardise interpretation across extractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish procedures for reliability and reaching consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Set procedures for assessing inter-rater reliability, resolving discrepancies, and reaching consensus when multiple authors extract data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use processes like independent extraction with reconciliation, third-party adjudication, or consensus meetings. Report how disagreements were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for extracting from multiple reports of the same study
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to link reports before extraction and extract across reports onto one form, or extract from each report and then link extracted data across reports; plan how to handle discrepancies across reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either strategy can be appropriate; document and justify the chosen approach. Use trial characteristics to link reports and contact authors if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracting from clinical study reports and regulatory reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: When using CSRs and regulatory reviews, extract detailed methods, appendices, and data tables following the same extraction framework but accounting for greater volume and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for longer time to obtain and analyse CSRs. CSRs often provide aggregate results and detailed harms data; maintain provenance and be explicit about which CSR documents were used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracting data from figures using software
rubrics_metrics.description: When numerical results are presented only in figures, use validated software/tools to capture and scale data from graphical representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Software extraction can be faster and more reliable than manual extraction; record methods and any assumptions or transformations used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automating data extraction where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider automation tools to assist data extraction but evaluate their performance and suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automation (machine learning, natural language processing) can assist but requires validation; consider human checking and reporting of automation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle suspicions of scientific misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Have procedures for when suspicions of fabrication, manipulation, or misconduct arise during data extraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate through errata, correspondence, and examination of inconsistencies; consider excluding unreliable studies and document reasons in excluded studies. Consult guidance on handling misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key items to report in methods about data extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: The methods section of the protocol and review should detail: data categories to extract; how extracted data will be verified; who will extract data; pilot testing/training/coding instructions; how data from multiple reports will be extracted; and how disagreements are handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting these items ensures transparency and reproducibility of data collection methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extracting study results and converting formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract summary data separately for each intervention group and enter into suitable software for effect estimation; where required data are not directly available, calculate or convert from reported formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6 contains techniques for common situations. Prefer computer-based conversions that retain original and computed values. Where adjusted analyses are required (e.g. cluster or crossover trials), extract effect estimates used in analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managing, archiving, and sharing extracted data
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize collected data electronically (databases/spreadsheets), retain provenance, perform cleaning and consistency checks, and archive data for future updates and sharing when legal/ethical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardize and share data collection tools and datasets when possible to reduce duplication. Store data in secure, stable locations and document transformations; when possible, make data publicly available to allow verification and reuse.
